input: Test the thesis: data-center power demand supports Vistra's growth over the next 3 years

output.thesis: Data-center power demand will support Vistra Corp.'s (NYSE: VST) growth over the next 3 years (roughly late 2026 through 2029).

evidence_for.claim: Vistra raised its 2026 midpoint and narrowed Ongoing Operations Adjusted EBITDA guidance to $7.1B–$7.5B, up from $5,912M in FY2025. It started 2027 guidance at $7.7B–$8.5B Adj. EBITDA and $4.3B–$5.1B Adj. FCFbG. Q3 2026 Ongoing Ops Adj. EBITDA was $2,378M, against $1,581M in Q3 2025. (as_of 2026-11-06)

In early 2026 Meta signed 20-year PPAs for more than 2,600 MW of energy, capacity and nuclear uprates at Vistra's PJM nuclear plants. The PPAs also support 20-year license renewals for all four PJM units. Meta was excluded from the Feb-2026 2027 'opportunity' figure of $7.4B–$7.8B. (as_of 2026-02-26)

Management says the Meta nuclear contract will begin contributing to 2027 results, and the 2027 guidance includes the Meta agreement and Cogentrix. The initiated 2027 range ($7.7B–$8.5B) sits above the earlier ex-Meta and ex-Cogentrix 'opportunity' range ($7.4B–$7.8B). (as_of 2026-11-06)

Comanche Peak has a 20-year PPA for up to 1,200 MW with AWS, and Amazon is building a roughly $5B data center next to the plant. In August 2026 executives said the Texas pause should not affect the deal and that the data center was on track to energize in 2027. (as_of 2026-08-10)

In Q3 2026 Vistra announced a 20-year, 207 MW PPA with New Era Energy and Digital at its Odessa gas plant in Texas. The 405 MW Pulaski solar facility began operating under a PPA with Microsoft. (as_of 2026-11-06)

Management expects Adj. FCFbG per share to rise from just under $10.50 (2025) to about $14 (2027). It also says it has 'line of sight to approximately 70% growth' in FCFbG per share from 2027 to 2030. Load growth is still forecast at 4–6% a year in ERCOT and 2–3% in PJM through 2030. (as_of 2026-11-06)

There is more to contract. Beaver Valley's nuclear output is still uncontracted ('we have a lot of megawatts still to contract on nuclear'), as are the second part of Comanche Peak and an uprate there. Talks are also under way on existing and new gas plants. The Permian Peakers and the coal-to-gas conversions are expected to contribute from 2028. (as_of 2026-11-06)

The SEC filings split the 2,609 MW of Meta PPAs into 2,176 MW of existing output and 433 MW of uprates. Deliveries of existing output start in late 2026 and are complete by the end of 2027. (as_of 2026, per secondary summary of 10-K/10-Q; not verified on an opened filing page)

evidence_against.claim: CEO Burke said 'ERCOT prices, however, have been trending lower,' and blamed crypto miners going offline to convert to data centers plus the Texas permitting pause. The 2027–2030 outlook assumes current forward curves and no price recovery. Vistra is 'much less hedged in ERCOT than the 78%' it reports for 2028. (as_of 2026-11-06)

On Aug. 3, 2026, Gov. Abbott ordered an audit of data center projects in the ERCOT queue and paused new connections. BNEF estimates up to 49.8 GW of ERCOT data center demand could be delayed and the audit could run until about April 2027. ERCOT's 474 GW large-load queue is about 5x its 91.3 GW peak. (as_of 2026-08-06)
Vistra cut its ERCOT annual load growth forecast to 4–6% from 5–6%. (as_of 2026-08-10)

On Sept. 21, 2026, Abbott told the TCEQ to stop issuing data center permits until ERCOT finishes its audit. No date for resuming permits was set. Burke said the hold 'might be lifted' around mid-December. He also said a Texas moratorium would be 'problematic' for Comanche Peak, though he does not see one as likely. (as_of 2026-09 / 2026-11-06)

A large share of near-term growth comes from M&A and buybacks rather than data-center contracts. Cogentrix (about 5,500 MW of gas, roughly $2.2B cash plus about $1.7B of assumed debt repaid) closed in October 2026, and Lotus (2,600 MW) closed in November 2025. About $2.5B of buyback authorization remains, and the 2030 per-share path assumes about $3B a year of buybacks. The 2027 FCFbG midpoint ($4.7B) is only slightly above the 2026 midpoint ($4.5B). (as_of 2026-11-06)

Contracted data-center volumes ramp slowly. The final ramp of the AWS Comanche Peak PPA is assumed in 2032. The Meta uprate MW (and the PJM uprate earnings) fall largely after 2030 and are excluded from the 2030 outlook. (as_of 2026-11-06)

Grid interconnection timing is a constraint on gas-plant data-center deals. Some customers will pay for temporary behind-the-meter power until grid service is available. PJM's reliability backstop procurement has been delayed. (as_of 2026-11-09)

Q3 2026 revenue was $6.35B against a $7.11B consensus. Vistra also took a $269M partial impairment on Moss Landing 350. Nine-month debt issuance was $7,985M, and pro forma liquidity fell to about $5.4B after Cogentrix and the preferred redemption. (as_of 2026-11-06/09)

counterarguments: The headline growth (2025 EBITDA $5.9B → 2027 guidance midpoint $8.1B) owes a lot to acquisitions (Cogentrix, Lotus) and to hedges already in place. Per-share growth leans heavily on buybacks of about $3B a year. Growth that comes specifically from data-center contracts is a smaller, slower-ramping part of the total (Comanche Peak full ramp in 2032; Meta uprates 2031–2034).

Data-center demand is currently pushing ERCOT prices down, not up. Crypto miners are going offline to convert, and the Texas audit and permit hold are delaying new load. With about 98% of 2027 hedged but much less than 78% of ERCOT hedged for 2028, Texas pricing in 2028–2029 is a real risk to the 3-year path (Fool transcript, 2026-11-06).

Texas policy has moved toward restriction: the Aug-2026 audit and connection pause, the Sept-2026 TCEQ permit halt, SB6 rulemaking, and a legislative session starting January 2027. BNEF says delays could run into April 2027, and Vistra has already cut its ERCOT load growth forecast (PowerMag, Utility Dive).

ERCOT's 474 GW queue is about 5x peak demand, and management itself calls the queues 'overstated.' Realized data-center load may come in well below the headlines, which caps how far the uncontracted merchant fleet can benefit.
key_uncertainties: When the ERCOT data-center audit and the TCEQ permit hold end (management expects about mid-December 2026; BNEF says possibly April 2027), and whether the 2027 Texas Legislature adds a moratorium or tighter large-load rules.
The ERCOT forward curve for 2028–2029, and how much of Vistra's ERCOT generation stays unhedged. The exact ERCOT hedge percentage for 2028 is not disclosed.
Whether Vistra signs Beaver Valley, the second part of Comanche Peak, or new-build gas PPAs, and at what price (management's hurdle is mid-teens levered returns).

The actual energization date and ramp schedule for the AWS Comanche Peak load (said to be on track for 2027, with full ramp in 2032) and the Meta delivery schedule. Management's comments on whether Meta's first deliveries come from Perry or Davis-Besse are inconsistent.
PJM market design (the delayed reliability backstop, co-location rules after FERC's June 2026 order) and its effect on bilateral data-center contracting.
How much of 2026–2029 EBITDA growth comes from data-center contracts versus M&A, hedges, and capacity prices. Vistra does not disclose this split.
what_would_change_the_view: Stronger: Vistra signs a long-term data-center PPA for Beaver Valley or the rest of Comanche Peak, or a new-build gas PPA, at mid-teens-plus returns.
Stronger: ERCOT ends the audit and connection pause by Q1 2027, Batch Zero large loads move ahead, and ERCOT 2028–2029 forwards rise.
Stronger: AWS's Comanche Peak data center energizes on schedule in 2027, and Meta deliveries reach full existing-output volumes by the end of 2027.
Weaker: the 2027 Texas Legislature passes a data-center moratorium or rules that block co-location or behind-the-meter supply, or the audit runs well past April 2027.
Weaker: ERCOT forward prices keep falling, or Vistra cuts its 4–6% ERCOT load growth forecast again or lowers its 2027 guidance.
Weaker: AWS or Meta delays or ends contracted deliveries, or the Meta uprates hit their termination conditions.
output.verdict: Partly supported. Signed data-center PPAs (Meta about 2.6 GW in PJM, AWS 1.2 GW at Comanche Peak, plus a 207 MW deal at Odessa and the Microsoft PPA at Pulaski) are real and already built into 2027 guidance of $7.7B–$8.5B EBITDA. That gives Vistra contracted, multi-decade revenue that underpins growth from the 2025 base of $5.9B. Much of the 3-year growth, though, comes from acquisitions, buybacks and hedges. The contracted data-center volumes ramp slowly (through 2032–2034). In Texas, data-center dynamics are currently pushing prices down, and policy risk (the audit, the permit hold, and the 2027 legislative session) makes the 2028–2029 merchant upside uncertain.
